intro: The Pali Canon is not one kind of book. It is a whole library of kinds: rules, talks, lists, short verses, songs and stories. In this unit, you will look closely at the genres of the Pali Canon and at how each one teaches in its own way.

First you will open the three baskets: the Sutta Pitaka with its five Nikayas, the Vinaya with its rules and their stories, and the Abhidhamma with its careful lists. Then you will read verse wisdom, nuns' songs and Jataka tales, and meet the commentators and translators who shaped how they are read.

By the end, you will be able to name the parts of the Pali Canon, explain how a sutta and a Jataka are built, compare two genres, and cite passages from public-domain translations like Rhys Davids (1881), Müller (1881) and Cowell (1895–1907).
bigQuestion: How do the different genres of the Pali Canon teach, and how have Buddhists and scholars read them?

timeline.t: Many scholars date the Buddha's death to about this time; the teachings are memorized
Jataka scenes are carved at Bharhut and, a little later, on the Sanchi gateways
Sri Lankan chronicles say the Pali Canon is written down in the 1st century BCE
Buddhaghosa writes commentaries in Sri Lanka
The Theravada line of fully ordained nuns dies out
Rhys Davids' Buddhist Suttas and Müller's Dhammapada appear in SBE
The Pali Text Society is founded in London
The Cowell Jataka is published in six volumes
Francis and Thomas publish Jataka Tales
Some Theravada monks begin ordaining women as nuns again

words.d: the basket of the Buddha's talks
one of five collections of talks
the basket of rules for monks and nuns
the core list of monastic rules
the basket of lists about mind and experience
a story of one of the Buddha's past lives
a text that explains another text
a kind of writing with its own shape and purpose
passing texts down by memory and speech
the teaching that all things change

test.q: Which basket holds the Buddha's talks?
What does a Vinaya rule usually come with?
choices: The story of why it was made

test.q: How many rules do Theravada nuns keep?
test.why: The Theravada bhikkhuni Patimokkha has 311 rules.
It sorts mind and experience into lists.

test.q: Why do the suttas repeat phrases?
choices: To make them longer for sale

test.q: Who translated the Dhammapada for Sacred Books of the East in 1881?
What does Dhammapada 5 say ends hatred?
test.why: In Müller's words, hatred ceases by love.

test.q: Who sings about her gray hair in the Therigatha?
test.why: Ambapali's song compares youth and age.

test.q: How many stories are in the Pali Jataka?
In a Jataka, what does the link do?
choices: Tells where the text was printed
Names who each past character was
test.why: The link joins the past story to the present.
He wrote the Visuddhimagga and many commentaries.

test.q: What did the Pali Text Society do?
choices: Printed Pali texts in Roman letters
test.why: Founded in 1881, it made printed editions and translations.

test.q: Who does the Vinaya say was the first nun?
test.why: Mahapajapati, the Buddha's aunt, asked to be ordained.

test.q: What image links the Makhadeva Jataka and Ambapali's song?
test.why: Both use gray hair to show impermanence.

write.prompt: Pick two genres from the Pali Canon, such as a verse and a Jataka, or a Vinaya rule and a nun's song. Cite a passage from each (for example Dhammapada 5, Müller 1881, or Jataka no. 9, Cowell 1895). Explain how each form teaches and how Buddhists have read it.
tips: Name each text, its number and its translation.
Say how the form (rule, verse, story, song) shapes the message.
Attribute beliefs: 'Theravada Buddhists teach...', 'the Jataka tells...'.
Compare, rather than judge, the two genres.
